title: Gravel in the Codru: Seven Days Through Moldova's Wine Hills
subRegion: Codru hills — Strășeni, Nisporeni, Călărași, Orhei

bestPeriod.window: the first three weeks of September — harvest, hard dry clay, and 25 °C instead of 35 °C
bestPeriod.avoid: March–April and November (clay tracks unrideable), and July–August (35 °C with no shade on the ridges)

transport.note: €110–€230 (bike rental €90–€180 or your own bike's flight surcharge, plus rutieră bail-outs)

activities.note: €70–€130 (monastery donations, reserve visit, cellar tours, Orheiul Vechi)

hook: The Codru is not flat and Moldova is not a road-bike country. This is 370 km of ridge-and-valley on a 35–40 mm tyre: resurfaced asphalt for an hour, then a slab of cracked Soviet concrete, then eight kilometres of packed clay farm track between vineyards with a monastery at the end of it. Climbs come in twenty-minute bites and add up to nearly 5,000 metres. Village wells, dogs, plum orchards, and almost no other cyclists.

snapshot.Getting there: Chișinău International (KIV), 13 km from town. Bring your own bike boxed if you can — rental stock in Moldova is thin and mostly hardtail MTB rather than gravel.

itinerary.title: Out of the capital, under it, and up
itinerary.morning: Leave Chișinău early on the northern exit towards Cricova; the first 8 km are urban and unpleasant, and after 07:30 they get worse. **Cricova** at 15 km — the 120 km cellar city, toured **by vehicle**, reservation-only, Matinal tour 250 MDL.
itinerary.afternoon: North-west on the R20 and then farm tracks through vineyards to **Strășeni**, the gateway town to the Codru. First real climb: the ridge out of the Ichel valley, 120 m in 2 km.
itinerary.evening: Strășeni is a working town, not a pretty one. Eat, buy tomorrow's water and food, and get the bike into a locked yard.

itinerary.title: Căpriana and the forest
itinerary.morning: Climb west into the **Codru forest** — hornbeam, oak and lime, closed canopy, and forest track that is fast when dry and greasy under leaf litter when not.
itinerary.afternoon: **Căpriana Monastery**, first documented in **1429** and the oldest in Moldova, restored in the 2000s: three churches, a walled compound, a spring, and a lot of Sunday visitors from the capital. Shoulders covered, and there is a shop selling monastery wine.
itinerary.evening: Down to **Lozova** at the reserve's edge. Village guesthouse, home cooking, and an early night — tomorrow is the biggest climbing day so far [VERIFY: current Căpriana monastery guesthouse and refectory arrangements].

itinerary.title: Reserve and the Hâncu ridge
itinerary.morning: The **Codru Nature Reserve** at Lozova: Moldova's oldest scientific reserve, with a natural history museum open daily 08:00–17:00. **Guided visits must be booked ahead** (tel 0237 47 386 / 0698 82 478) — it is not a walk-up, and the trails are not open access [VERIFY: current Codru reserve visit fee].
itinerary.afternoon: South-west on ridge track to **Hâncu Monastery** (Mănăstirea Hâncu, founded 1678) in its wooded fold — the descent to it is a 150 m drop on loose clay, so check your brakes at the top rather than halfway down.
itinerary.evening: North-west to **Nisporeni**, a district town with a hotel, a market and an ATM. Refill everything [VERIFY: current Nisporeni hotel rates and whether bike storage is indoors].

itinerary.title: The roof of Moldova
itinerary.morning: East to **Vărzărești**, whose monastery has a claim as one of the country's earliest foundations, then a long ridge line on farm track with the Prut plain visible to the west on a clear morning.
itinerary.afternoon: **Bălănești Hill (Dealul Bălănești)**, **430 m — the highest point in Moldova**, above Bălănești village. The final approach is a rutted field track; the summit is a mast and a marker, and the view over the Codru is genuinely worth the disappointment of the summit itself.
itinerary.evening: North-east down to **Călărași**, wine town and rail junction. This is the best-supplied stop after Chișinău — a proper supermarket, a bike-washable yard, and *rachiu* if you want it.

itinerary.title: Across to the Răut side
itinerary.morning: East on the R25 through orchard country. The concrete-slab sections start around here; ride the smoother wheel track and expect your hands to complain by lunch.
itinerary.afternoon: **Bahmut** and the long rolling transition out of the Codru proper — the hills lower, the tree cover thins, and the wind starts to matter more than the gradient.
itinerary.evening: **Ivancea**, and the **Balioz manor**, a restored 19th-century estate house holding a museum of Moldovan folk crafts, with a park you can lie down in [VERIFY: current Ivancea manor museum hours and entry].

itinerary.title: The Răut meander
itinerary.morning: Track north-east to the **Orheiul Vechi** reserve. The approach along the Răut, on clay above the river, is the single best hour of riding on this loop.
itinerary.afternoon: **Orheiul Vechi**: the cave monastery in the limestone spur above **Butuceni**, entry **20 MDL** adult / 10 MDL reduced, guide 200 MDL in Romanian or 300 MDL in English for up to ten people. Leave the bike at the guesthouse and walk the promontory.
itinerary.evening: Butuceni or **Trebujeni** guesthouse. Half board, house wine, and a sky with no light pollution in it.

itinerary.title: Home the fast way
itinerary.morning: Out along the river, then the climb onto the plateau at Furceni — 130 m, the last real effort of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: South-west on a mix of R-road asphalt and track through Bulăiești and Peresecina, joining the main road for the final approach to the city.
itinerary.evening: Into Chișinău on the northern boulevards. Clean the bike, then **Carpe Diem** or **Invino** for the Fetească Neagră you have been riding past all week.

accommodationStrategy.name: Lozova village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: at the Codru reserve gate, so the guided reserve visit is a morning walk rather than a drive, with a locked yard for the bikes, an outside tap for the clay and a kitchen that will feed you at whatever hour you arrive.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 weeks ahead by phone; ask the host to confirm the reserve booking for you in Romanian.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel in Călărași
accommodationStrategy.description: the mid-trip reset — the only place between Chișinău and Orhei with a supermarket, an ATM, a pharmacy and enough hot water for two bikes and two riders. Secure ground-floor storage, and the rail line here if you truly need to abandon.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 1–2 weeks ahead; midweek availability is never a problem.

accommodationStrategy.name: Butuceni village guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: inside the Orheiul Vechi reserve, five minutes from the cave monastery path, with a yard, half board and the Belvedere platform for sunrise before the day-trip coaches arrive from the capital.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead — the village has a few dozen beds and Chișinău takes them at weekends.

logistics.connectivity: Moldova is **not** in EU roaming — buy an Orange or Moldcell SIM at KIV. Coverage on the ridges is good; it drops in the Codru forest valleys. Load offline maps and a GPX before you leave, because signposting on farm track is nil.
logistics.emergency: **112**, English usually available. Give a village name and direction, not a GPS string. There is no cycling-specific rescue; ambulances will not reach you on a field track, so ride out to a road before calling if you can.
logistics.weather: Rain is the trip's only real hazard. A summer thunderstorm turns 40% of a day's route into unrideable gumbo within twenty minutes and it stays that way for a day or more. Watch the forecast every evening and be willing to swap a track day for the parallel asphalt R-road.
logistics.bookingWindows: Codru reserve, Cricova and any winery visit need a phone call days ahead. Guesthouses 2–4 weeks in season. A rented gravel bike, several weeks.
logistics.money: Moldovan leu. Cards work in Chișinău, Călărași and Nisporeni; village guesthouses, wells, monastery shops and roadside sellers are **cash only**. Carry 2,000–3,000 MDL and keep small notes for the rutieră.
logistics.transportRules: Ride on the right, lights front and rear, and use a **hi-vis vest** — it is expected of cyclists on rural roads at dusk and drivers here overtake close. Village dogs and free-roaming livestock are on every unfenced road.
logistics.permits: No permit for ordinary roads or forest tracks. **The Codru scientific reserve is by prior arrangement only** — do not simply ride into it. Orheiul Vechi charges 20 MDL. Wild camping is legally grey and socially odd; every village has a bed.

proTips: **The dog technique, learned properly.** Village dogs chase wheels, not people. **Stop pedalling and dismount** — most break off immediately. Put the bike between you and the dog, keep walking at the same pace, do not run, do not shout high, and say ***"Marș!"*** low and flat, which is the word every Moldovan dog has heard. Cross to the far side of the road and keep going. A frame pump held loosely is a deterrent you rarely need to use.

**Village wells (*fântână*) — use them, with judgement.** Almost every crossroads has one, usually with a bucket and often a shared cup, and locals drink from them daily. But shallow wells in this farmland carry **nitrate from fertiliser and livestock**, which no filter or purification tablet removes and which boiling concentrates. Prefer a deep well in the village centre that people are actively using, ask *"Se poate bea?"*, and carry bottled water for the second half of a hot day.

**The rutieră is your bail-out — with conditions.** Minibuses run every district road to Chișinău. Bikes are **at the driver's discretion**, usually accepted for a small extra fare if the bus is not full, and your odds improve enormously if you **take the front wheel off before he looks at it**. Sprinter-type vans have no luggage bay, so a full bus is a straight no. Flag it down at a village stop and ask *"Se poate cu bicicleta?"* [VERIFY: current rutieră bicycle surcharge].
**Ride the track days early.** Clay holds dew until nine and heat-cracks by noon; the ridges are 8 °C hotter at 14:00 with no shade whatever. Leave at 06:30 and be finished by two.
**Lube the chain every single evening.** Loess dust is abrasive and strips lubricant in a day; a dry chain on a 900 m climbing day is how drivetrains die 60 km from the nearest replacement.

**Buy from the gate.** Small producers along the Codru sell at a third of restaurant prices, and a guesthouse will happily open a bottle you turn up with. Send anything serious home rather than carrying it over Bălănești Hill.

**Book one rest afternoon at Orheiul Vechi.** It is the only place on the loop worth a half-day off the bike, and arriving in the morning of Day 6 rather than the evening buys you the promontory in good light.

raw.Daily distance, ascent and surface split: **Day 1** Chișinău → Cricova → Strășeni, **40 km / +450 m** — 70% asphalt, 20% concrete slab, 10% clay track. **Day 2** Strășeni → Căpriana → Lozova, **45 km / +700 m** — 40% asphalt, 15% slab, 45% forest and farm track. **Day 3** Lozova → Codru reserve → Hâncu → Nisporeni, **55 km / +850 m** — 50% asphalt, 10% slab, 40% track. **Day 4** Nisporeni → Vărzărești → Bălănești Hill → Călărași, **60 km / +900 m** — 45% asphalt, 15% slab, 40% track. **Day 5** Călărași → Bahmut → Ivancea, **65 km / +750 m** — 60% asphalt, 20% slab, 20% track. **Day 6** Ivancea → Orheiul Vechi loop, **45 km / +550 m** — 40% asphalt, 10% slab, 50% track. **Day 7** Orheiul Vechi → Chișinău, **60 km / +600 m** — 65% asphalt, 15% slab, 20% track.
raw.This is a gravel trip, and only a gravel: **35–40 mm tyres minimum**, tubeless or with two spare tubes, and a frame with mud clearance. Moldovan farm track is fine-grained loess and clay: it is fast, hard and lovely when dry, and after rain it becomes ***gumbo*** — a sticky paste that packs solid between tyre and fork until the wheel stops turning and you carry the bike. A 28 mm road bike will get you between towns on asphalt and nowhere else. The **Codru is genuine ridge-and-valley terrain**, 200–430 m, and the climbing arrives as repeated 60–120 m ramps at 8–12% on loose surface — riders consistently underestimate it.
raw.Bike rental and logistics: Chișinău has a handful of bike shops and small tour operators renting mostly cross-country hardtails; a true gravel bike is hard to source and should be reserved weeks ahead by email. Assume you will need to bring your own pedals, saddle and shoes regardless [VERIFY: current Chișinău gravel-bike rental operators and daily rates].
raw.No bike shops outside Chișinău — plan fo: Once you leave the capital there is no spares network. Village hardware shops sell inner tubes for Soviet-era 28-inch wheels and nothing else. Carry: two tubes, tubeless plugs, a spare **derailleur hanger**, quick links, spare spokes, brake pads, a folding tyre, chain lube (the clay strips it), and a mini pump plus CO2. A broken hanger 60 km from Chișinău otherwise ends the trip.
raw.Bike-friendly accommodation features: Village *pensiuni* almost all have a locked yard, a shed or a *beci* (cellar) you can wheel a bike into, an outside tap for washing off clay, and a line to dry kit. Ask for *"un loc pentru bicicletă"* when booking; nobody will refuse.
raw.Trains and buses with a bike: Moldova's passenger rail network is minimal and not useful for this loop. The practical bail-out is the ***rutieră*** minibus — see below.
